items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I joined Lee Collins and David Jones’s band.

ctx.x: Wiggins. A great piano player. Played with him. And I played with Lee Collins and them. That’s where I graduate to big time. I joined Lee Collins and David Jones’s band. I taken [Emmanuel] Sayles’s place. They had scanned banjo players around there.

That’s why they called me to the rehearsal they had. Lee Collins look at me. I had on these $20 [? (inaudible)] shoes [? (inaudible)]. Later on he said, “You know why I hired you?” He said, “You wasn’t playing much banjo. I hired you because you had on them pretty shoes. I used to like to look at them shoes, and I knew you’d amount to something some day.” That’s why he hired me in the band. I went in the band and that’s where I heard some [expletive deleted]. Me, Roy . . . now who the hell was on bass?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Joe Robichaux. Fats Martin on drums. We had Earl(?) Pernell on clarinet and saxophone. David Jones on tenor. Ernest Kelly on trombone.

ctx.x: Well, Joe Robichaux played piano. Joe Robichaux. Fats Martin on drums. We had Earl(?) Pernell on clarinet and saxophone. David Jones on tenor. Ernest Kelly on trombone. Ernest Kelly was a great man to play the Dozens. He'd actually talk about your mother in an uncouth
